perennials/381245a:
PlantCard printed warnings[0], the first of a coarse vocabulary that exists
only for filtering. model.ts says never to show it to a human: "Toxic fruits"
and "Toxic for cats" both flatten to "Toxic". Because the label that sorted
first won, seven edible plants hid their toxicity outright -- chokecherry
showed "Weed potential" and never mentioned the poisonous seeds, while listing
Seed as edible. Castor bean rendered "Edible" beside "Toxic".

Lead with the clause that can hurt her, in the source's words, and fall back
to the coarse label only when the verbatim clause cannot fit the chip. Across
all 791 warned plants the longest chip is 18 characters and none lose theirs.

api: compress the payload and address the ETag to its content

plants.json went out at 8.88 MB with no content-encoding at all; brotli takes
it to 0.94 MB. The ETag hashed max(updated_at), which the hourly re-check
never writes, so the server served a new body under an old ETag and every
phone answered 304 forever -- ten weeks of re-verified flower visitors never
reached a device. Hash the bytes instead.
